description: Trigger discrimination for the Phase 5 strategy/plan/coverage cluster: one-change plan vs product strategy vs coverage audit vs automation tooling, plus discrimination against the shipped multi-tenant-security-tester for security-suite asks, and against integration-test-designer and test-coverage-mapper for negative-path mapping.

cases.prompt: We're shipping a new billing proration change next week — plan what we test, with what data, and when testing is done.
cases.reason: A single change's scope, data, and exit criteria is a per-change plan, not product strategy or tooling design.

cases.prompt: Decide which test layers this product needs long-term and who owns each.
cases.reason: Long-term layer investment and ownership is strategy; no single change is in view.

cases.prompt: Before we plan anything new — what do our existing tests actually cover for billing?
cases.reason: Auditing current coverage is the mapper; planning new verification comes after.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke multi-tenant-security-tester. Plan and specify the cross-tenant negative tests proving tenant A can't read tenant B's invoices.
cases.reason: Cross-tenant/authorization negative suites are owned by the shipped multi-tenant-security-tester; test plans reference its output as line items.

cases.prompt: Map every negative path for this API change: the new POST /invites endpoint and the billing webhook handler.
cases.reason: Walking the seven negative-path classes per touched surface for one change is the plan's negative-path matrix; cross-tenant cells are delegated line items, and integration-test-designer designs the boundary suites the plan hands off to.

cases.prompt: Map negative paths for this feature: bulk invoice export. What unauthorized, expired, duplicate and out-of-order cases should we plan for?
cases.reason: Planning which negative cases a feature needs, before tests exist, is the per-change plan; it is neither an integration-suite design nor an audit of existing coverage.
